_readme: Living status tracker. For architecture, history, and code documentation, see RoutineHub-Reloaded.md instead, since that file is narrative and changes slowly, while this one is structured data and changes constantly. colors_styling values are ok, needs_recheck, or broken. features status values are planned, implemented, open_todo, or note.

reset.reason: RoutineHub replaced the navbar menu entirely, from a flat dropdown list to a categorized slide out sidebar, Home, account name, Community, Create New, a collapsible Channels section with a New and Updated channel not seen before, a collapsible Account section with Settings, CreatorHub, My Purchases, and a new HubSign item, plus a promotional banner and social icons. The CSS build filename has also changed twice more since the last stylesheet audit. Every page colors_styling value was reset to needs_recheck again as a result, on the explicit assumption that if the navbar changed this much, other pages likely did too.
reset.note: The new sidebar only renders for an authenticated session. A live automated check without login only reaches the old flat menu. Raw HTML from the user is needed before building any fix for this specific component, rather than guessing selectors from a screenshot or the compiled CSS alone, since neither reliably confirms the real class names.

top_findings: rh-comment and rh-comment-thread look like a separate comment system from the #feedback and article.media based one built for the shortcut page. Not confirmed yet, needs investigating.
rh-segmented is a native segmented control component. Directly relevant to the planned Authored view mode switcher, since Grid, List, Detailed is exactly that kind of control.
rh-skill prefixed classes point to a Skill detail page, structurally parallel to the shortcut detail page, previously unknown to this project.
rh-checkin-board appeared in the 2026-09-11 run. Looks like a leaderboard or shared view of check ins across multiple users, separate from the existing single user check in card.

A large rh-box and rh-boxes family appeared in the 2026-09-11 run with terminology like state creating, state queued, state ready, and an SSH command panel. Suggests some kind of sandbox or cloud environment feature. Flagged as unclear, not guessed at further.

cross_cutting.name: Theme trigger logic
cross_cutting.description: Done and verified live in version 1.0.0-alpha22, in both Chromium and WebKit. Replaced the prefers-color-scheme media query with a JS driven .rhe-dark class on the html element, computed as OS prefers dark or their data-theme=dark, kept live via a matchMedia listener and a MutationObserver on the attribute. Confirmed the exact previously identified gap is closed, forcing data-theme=dark while OS is light now flips a real page's card background to our own color live, no reload.

cross_cutting.name: Toggle icon mismatch
cross_cutting.description: Done and verified live in version 1.0.0-alpha22. Their dark state toggle visuals turned out to be plain html[data-theme=dark] CSS with hardcoded values, not aria-checked driven, so those exact values were re-keyed onto .rhe-dark, and aria-checked itself now syncs to the actual effective theme. Verified the exact reported scenario, OS dark with their attribute forced to light, and confirmed the icon renders fully dark while their data-theme attribute stays untouched underneath.

reset_log.reason: RoutineHub shipped their own native dark mode using a data-theme=dark attribute on the html element, with roughly 731 rule blocks in the CSS build active at the time. This happened between the last full sweep and now. Every page colors_styling value was reset to needs_recheck as a result. Features status is not affected by the reset, since a feature's JS and UX behavior does not depend on the site's own CSS changing.
reset_log.note: Historical last_checked dates are mostly not recorded precisely. Only relative order, via alpha version numbers, is reliably known for anything before this reset date. Where a real date is not known, last_checked is null rather than guessed.
